title: The MLS Wrap: Son can’t stop LAFC slump while Revs overtake Messi’s Miami
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Son can’t stop LAFC slump while Revs overtake Messi’s MiamiShareThe latest round of MLS matches came amid a moment of celebration for several first-time call-ups to Mauricio Pochettino’s United States team, including one for the league’s standout young star, Cavan Sullivan.

A few of those young players put in notable performances in the latest round of MLS matches, but it was Sullivan and his Philadelphia Union team who once again stole the limelight with a sensational comeback win in Kansas.
Was a wondergoal from Son Heung-min enough to give LAFC a much-needed win? And which team has come up on the rails to overtake Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami?
The latest MLS Wrap answers these questions and has the latest headlines, as well as unearthing some of the more under-the-radar stories in the North American league.
There have been points throughout the last three years when you simply can’t do a weekly roundup of MLS without mentioning Inter Miami and Messi.
The individual performances, coinciding with a team regularly winning games and challenging at the top of the table, meant they could not be ignored.
Even if you try to mix it up to give all the teams some coverage at some point, Messi and Miami demand inclusion most weeks.
Few other players have put in consecutive performances that necessitate such constant attention for their team, but one who is doing so currently is Cavan Sullivan at Philadelphia Union.

The Union’s run since Ryan Richter took over as interim coach is outstanding. They are yet to lose an MLS game during his tenure, and this weekend took that unbeaten run to 11 games in the league, featuring nine wins.

Their run of consecutive wins currently stands at five games thanks to a remarkable 4-3 win against Sporting Kansas City this weekend, coming back to take all three points despite having gone 3-0 down.
What's more, all four of their goals were scored in the space of ten second-half minutes.
A Sporting KC collapse or an unbelievable Philadelphia Union comeback?
Either way, Sullivan, who scored one of those goals to take him to six in his last six games, and the Union are in the headlines once again.

They haven’t stormed up the table like Philadelphia Union, and aren’t one of those teams having a season of two halves that can be separated neatly into pre and post-World Cup narratives, but New England Revolution have gone about the business of winning more games than they lose or draw in 2026, and have sneaked above Inter Miami in the table as a result.
They also boast a teenage American star of their own in 18-year-old Peyton Miller.
The winger scored twice in this weekend’s 4-2 win against Orlando City, building on the one he scored last week against Chicago Fire, and on the three assists in three games he managed in August.
Precise finishes on the break showed his composure even when running at speed with plenty of time to think. Not bad for a player who started out as a left-back.
On the back of such performances, he received a deserved first call-up to the USMNT for the upcoming international window.

The Revolution also have Carles Gil, who has consistently been one of the best players in MLS for eight seasons now, regardless of the kind of form in which the New England team as a whole have been in those years.

Gil contributed a brace of his own to go with Miller’s, and if they can continue with this combination of individual talent and teamwork and results, they may well remain above Inter Miami for the rest of the season and be a threat in the playoffs.
